newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Kreditni officials released from jail - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech Kreditni officials released from jail - agency.

text.p: Five executives arrested in connection with the failure of Czech Kreditni Banka a.s. have been released from jail, the news agency CTK reported on Friday.

CTK quoted regional court officials as saying the five, who were implicated in a fraud scheme which caused losses at the bank totalling at least 2.88 billion crowns ($108.6 million), had been released, though they did not say why.
The five were charged in mid-September with fraud, damage to creditors, and abetting fraud.
The bank's licence was withdrawn by the Czech National Bank in August with losses estimated at nearly 12 billion crowns.

The failure of Kreditni Banka, a medium-sized bank based in Plzen, caused a political furore over bank supervision, and led parliament to create a special commission to lead an investigation into the case.

Kreditni was the 11th of the country's then-over 50 banks to fail, and led to Agrobanka, the fifth-largest bank, to be placed under temporary central bank administration due to liquidity problems arising from Kreditni's situation.

Local media reports have placed the blame for the failure of Kreditni Banka, majority-owned by the largest insurer Ceska Pojistovna a.s., on a series of murky loans made to interests connected to shareholders.
Pojistovna, which took majority stake in Kreditni in 1994, when the bank was reportedly already in a bad situation, has said it was liable for a total of nearly six billion crowns lost at Kreditni.
Kreditni's shareholders, after the central bank shut it in August, voted to liquidate the bank.
